title: Tarte Tatin
subtitle: Upside-down caramelised apple tart with puff pastry
excerpt: Apples cooked in a rich, darkly caramelised butter-and-sugar sauce in an oven-proof pan, then covered with puff pastry and baked, and finally inverted to reveal a gleaming tarte of golden apples.

recipe.sourceNotes: Tarte Tatin is a French upside-down apple tart that takes its name from the Tatin sisters, Stephanie and Caroline, who ran a hotel-restaurant in Lamotte-Beuvron in the Loire Valley in the late nineteenth century. According to the most popular account, the tart was created by accident when Stephanie Tatin began cooking the apple filling without a pastry base and, to save the dish, placed the pastry on top and flipped the tart on serving. The recipe was popularised nationally by the Parisian restaurant Maxim's. The dish is made in a heavy oven-proof pan: the caramel and apples are cooked together on the hob, the pastry is laid on top, and then the whole pan goes in the oven. The tart must be inverted while still hot, before the caramel sets and sticks the apples to the pan. Cox or Braeburn apples hold their shape best and give good acidity against the caramel.

recipeTools.notes: A 24 cm oven-proof frying pan or cast-iron pan with no plastic handle.

content.text: The caramel will look alarming at the point of adding the apples: it will seize and harden around them. Keep the heat steady and the caramel will reliquify as the apples release their juice. The pastry should be tucked down around the inside edge of the pan before baking. The tart must be inverted within 2 minutes of coming out of the oven: leave it longer and the caramel sets and the apples stick to the pan. Place the serving plate over the pan, hold both firmly, and flip in one clean motion.

items.preparation: Cox or Braeburn; peeled, cored, quartered
rolled to a 26 cm circle, chilled

content.text: Heat the oven to 200 C / fan 180 C / gas 6. Melt the sugar in a 24 cm oven-proof frying pan over medium-high heat without stirring until it forms a dark amber caramel. Add the butter and stir until melted. Add the vanilla.

Arrange the apple quarters tightly in the caramel, curved-side down in a ring around the edge and filling the centre. Cook on the hob over medium heat for 10 minutes until the apples soften slightly and the caramel bubbles up around them.
Lay the pastry circle over the apples and tuck the edges down around the inside of the pan. Bake for 25 to 28 minutes until the pastry is deeply golden and the caramel is bubbling up at the edges.

Leave to cool for just 2 minutes. Place a large serving plate over the pan. Invert firmly in one motion. Lift the pan off. Rearrange any apple quarters that have moved. Serve warm with creme fraiche or vanilla ice cream.
